chunks.rationale: Start with paneLayout.test.ts (the tree ops). Then paneWorkspace.test.tsx for close/Cmd+\/drag. Then threadHeader Views cases, especially the two persistence tests: empty→thread restore, and A→B isolation.
risks: jsdom has no DragEvent; drag-swap uses a module-level draggingPaneId plus generic Event('dragstart'|'drop')
unmountAll wipes coder.paneLayout.* after each test; persistence-across-remount is asserted inside a single test before afterEach

chunks.rationale: Layout is owned per threadId. ThreadView adjusts layout during render when detail.thread.id !== layoutThreadId (React's 'store previous render' pattern) so we never persist thread A's tree under B's key, and empty→thread reloads storage instead of a chat-only default.
risks: setState during render must only run when the ids differ; a loop here would freeze the pane
the changesOpen effect must NOT list threadId in its deps or a stale changesOpen=true on the first frame after a switch would force Git open on the new thread

chunks.rationale: PaneWorkspace renders the binary split tree. Views menu lives in the session toolbar. Chat and Git are real panes; other registry types are placeholders. Exclusive Thread|Git tabs are gone. When the pane chrome is showing, ChangesPanel hides its own 'Git' title (embedded).
risks: changesOpen is an open-request, not exclusive visibility
PaneWorkspace class leafBody (not body) so CSS-module tests that query('.body') still hit the transcript scroller

chunks.rationale: KeyboardSheet gained ⌘ + \. Cmd+\ is renderer-only on purpose: adding an Electron View-menu accelerator would double-fire with the window keydown and close two panes.
risks: Shortcut is missing from the native View menu; KeyboardSheet is the discovery path
Sidebar and Agents stay app chrome, not pane types.
Layout lives in localStorage (coder.paneLayout.<threadId>), not coder-store.json.
No browser verification of drag/resize; jsdom has no layout.
